newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to liberalise overseas investments in Aug.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to liberalise overseas investments in Aug.

text.p: South Korea said on Thursday it would liberalise overseas direct investments from August 1.
A finance ministry statement said companies that wanted to invest in foreign countries would be allowed to do so by making a report to their designated foreign-exchange bank.
Applicants are currently obliged to obtain the central Bank of Korea's approval for overseas capital projects exceeding $50 million.
The ministry also said it would end from August 1 requirements that companies use some of their own capital in financing overseas investments.

Currently, more than 10 percent of an overseas investment should be financed by a company's own capital if the investment is $100 million or less and more than 20 percent if it exceeds $100 million, the ministry said.
But the ministry said the government would continue screening projects where capital provided by investing companies was deemed to be inadequate.
Projects designated for screening would include those thought to be too ambitious given a company's financial status.
For example, an overseas investment deliberation committee would examine projects that require more than 50 percent of a company's net worth or paid-in capital.
Overseas investments by South Korean companies totalled $6.18 billion in 1996 for 1,774 projects, compared with $4.91 billion in 1,556 projects in 1995.
During the first four months of this year, such investments were $1.82 billion, against $1.95 billion a year ago, the ministry said.
